Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

tensile strength of 550 MPs end satisfying band test ss in 7.1.

5. General Requirements — The nails shall be machine mada and may have die marks and feeding 
knife marks on the ahank. They shall be uniformly circular in section, straight, free from wasters and 
the enda shall be pointed to conform to the dimensions given In Tablaa 1 t( > 4 * The heads shall be 
properly tormea, chequered and concentric with the shank. 

§. Finish — Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser countersunk head wire nails shall be 
supplied bright finished. 

7. Teel 

7.1 B*nd Test — Steel countersunk head wire nails, selected according to 9.2, when cold ahall not 
break or develop cracks, when doubled over either by pressure or by blow from a hammer untill the 
internal radius is eaual to the diameter of the test piece and the sides are parallel.

S. Packing — Nails of different sizes and types shall be packed In separate containers. 

9.1 Nails including 25 mm In length and below shall be packed In cardboard boxes and the net weight 
of each box shall be 0*5 kg. The nails may alto be supplied in gunny bags, and the net weight of each 
bag shall be 60 kg. 

9.2 Nails above 26 mm and below 80 mm in length shall be packed in cardboard boxes and the net 
weight of each box shall be 2*5 kg. The nails may also be supplied in gunny bags, and the net weight 
of each bag shall be 60 kg. 

8.3 Nails 80 mm and ebove in length shall be packed in wrappings of double gunny bags, the weight 
of the each package being 15 kg. The nails may also be supplied in .cases of bituminized canvae or 
hessian bags; the net weight of each package shall be 50 ka. 

8. Scale of Sampling and Criteria for Conformity 

8.1 Lot -~ In any consignment all the packages of neils of the same type and size manufactured under 
essentially similar conditions shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

8.2 Select/on of Samples — The number of nails to be selected at random from the lot shall depend on 
the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 6. The nails shall be selected 
from at least 26 percent of the packages. 

8.S Visual and Dimensional Character/sties 

8.3.1 Number of tests and criteria for conformity— All the nails selected as in 8.2 shell be examined 
for manufacturing defects, dimensions and finish. 

8.3.2 The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of these characterstics if the 
number of nails examined for characteristics mentioned in 8.3.1 and found defective does not exceed the 
corresponding acceptance number given in col 3 of Table 5.

Note— The sampling plan accepts tho lots containing 7 percsnt or lets defectives In

9.4 Bend Test 

9.4.1 Number of tests and criteria for conformity— The number of nails to be selected for carrying out 
bend test shall be according to col 4 of Table 5. These nails shall be selected from those already 
inspected according to 9.3.1 and found satisfactory. 

The lot shall be considered aa conforming to the requirements of bend test if the number of 
nails failing to pass this test does not exceed the corresponding acceptance number in cot 6 of Table 5. 

9.5 The lot ahall be considered ea conforming to the requirements of the specification if it satisfies 9.3.1 
and 9.4,1.

10. Marking — All packages of 'naila shall bs marked with the following information: 

a) Manufacturer's nams or trade-mark, 

b) Type of nail, 

c) Size ( shank diameter ) and length of nail, and 

d) Net weight of the package. 

10.1 ISI CwUfteatton Making — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

The specification for mild steel wire nails was first revised in 1 961. In the present revision the 
following changes have been made: 

a) The angle of countersunk has been increased from 90° to 1 20°. 

b) Nail head diameter has been changed to 2d for shank diameters ranging between 2*0 to 
2*8 mm and to 1 *8d for shank diameters above 2*8 mm. 

c) Tolerancea for eccentricity and ovality of nail heads has been specified. 

d) Provision for galvanized finish nails has been deleted and plain finish haa been specified. 

e) The sampling plan haa been suitably modified to permit allowable percentage of defective 
naila from 4 percent to 7 percent. 

f) The present revision covers only countersunk heed wire nells.' The other types are being 
covered by separate standards, as follows: 

IS: 6730-1972 Felt naila 

IS : 6732-1972 Double point naila 

IS : 6733-1972 Wall and roofing naila 

IS : 6734-1972 Cut lajth and lath naila 

IS : 6738-1972 Panel pins and lost heed naila
